newsitem.title: SYRIA: Not clear who shot two Austrian soldiers in Syria.
newsitem.headline: Not clear who shot two Austrian soldiers in Syria.

text.p: The commander of Austrian U.N. troops in the Golan Heights said on Saturday two Austrian soldiers were killed inside Syrian territory but investigations had not identified who was responsible.
"The shooting occured in the Syrian territory.. we have not reached any result yet as to who was responsible," Nicolas Eggar told Reuters.
"We have started the investigation but we do not know who did it or when we might reach a result about that. And we might not reach any result at all," he said.

He said the bodies of the junior officer and the soldier serving with the United Nation Disengagement Observer Force (UNDOF) would be sent to Austria on Wednesday. They are in a Damascus military hospital.
The Austrian defence ministry said in Vienna the two soldiers were shot dead on Friday during a foot patrol on the Golan Heights between Syria and Israel.
The Israeli army said on Friday the soldiers were shot eight km (five miles) from Israeli lines and Israeli troops were not involved.

UNDOF serves as a buffer between the Syrian and Israeli armies on the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in 1967. The 1,050-member force has been deployed since 1974 to monitor a ceasefire and troop withdrawal that followed the 1973 Middle East war.
Austria has more than 400 soldiers stationed on the Golan Heights.
